documents.title: Guidelines for Academic Use
documents.stance_why: The page sets no university-wide permission or ban. It says 'permitted uses of GAI may not be the same in every course' and 'instructors set expectations for their classes, and these expectations can differ', while requiring each syllabus to carry expectations. The decision is handed to instructors, so delegates; no named tiers or templates are offered.
documents.summary: University-wide guidelines adapted from the March 2025 AI Working Group for Academics report. They require course syllabi to state GAI expectations, leave permitted uses to instructors, and ask schools to update honor codes, treat detectors as insufficient proof, and ensure equitable access. A discussion framework asks programs to coordinate across courses.

units.why: The opening frames the page as an institution-level statement of purpose and scope: the guidelines 'articulate expectations and recommendations for academic work' grounded in the vision's principles. P56 (institution-wide framework) fits better than P61 because it states purpose, not definitions.
units.anchor: the following guidelines articulate expectations and recommendations for academic work

units.why: Headline guideline telling instructors to put GAI policy on every syllabus: 'Include GAI expectations and policies on each course syllabus'. The page calls its content 'expectations and recommendations', so modality is should; P09 matches exactly.
units.anchor: Include GAI expectations and policies on each course syllabus

units.why: Lists what a syllabus statement should cover: 'the types of resources students can use for which assignments; how and when GAI platforms may be used'. It is the content spec of the P09 syllabus requirement, not a separate rule about what is allowed.
units.anchor: the types of resources students can use for which assignments
units.policy: The syllabus statement addresses the types of resources students can use for which assignments, how and when GAI platforms may be used, how and when students can work together, and appropriate citation methods.

units.why: Gives the reason for syllabus statements: they 'provide clarity for all students and support their success'. Nearest type is P09 since it justifies the syllabus requirement.
units.anchor: Syllabus statements provide clarity for all students and support their success.
units.fit_note: Rationale for the syllabus requirement rather than the requirement itself.

units.why: Asks instructors to frame expectations in 'academic and professional integrity as well as support for student learning', i.e. to give the reasons rather than only list rules. P66 (explain the rules) is the closest type.
units.anchor: Situate these expectations within the larger context of academic and professional integrity
units.policy: Instructors situate GAI expectations within the larger context of academic and professional integrity as well as support for student learning.
units.fit_note: Asks for framing within integrity and learning support; does not mention discussing the rules with students.

units.why: 'Consult with peers and other professional resources for best practices' tells instructors to seek outside advice when writing policy. P63 (support faculty in learning AI) is nearest; P109 does not fit because it is about aligning rules, not seeking advice.
units.anchor: Consult with
units.policy: Instructors consult peers and other professional resources for best practices.
units.fit_note: Peer consultation by instructors rather than institutional workshops or support.

units.why: States that 'permitted uses of GAI may not be the same in every course or on every assignment', so one course's permission does not carry over. P11 chosen over P04 because the sentence says rules differ, while the next sentence assigns who decides.
units.anchor: the permitted uses of GAI may not be the same in every course or on
units.policy: Permitted uses of GAI may not be the same in every course or on every assignment in a course.

units.why: 'permitted uses of GAI may change over time' acknowledges that rules are provisional, which is P54.
units.anchor: permitted uses of GAI may change over time
units.policy: Permitted uses of GAI may change over time.

units.why: 'instructors set expectations for their classes, and these expectations can differ' places the decision with each instructor, bounded by academic freedom, course coordination and department policy. This is P04; the stance of the whole document is therefore delegates.
units.anchor: instructors set expectations for their classes, and these expectations can differ
units.policy: Within the overlapping frameworks of academic freedom, course coordination, and department/unit curriculum and policies, instructors set expectations for their classes, and these expectations can differ.

units.why: Argues why silence is a problem: 'absence of GAI guidance ... undermines the ability to recognize and adjudicate' misconduct. It supports the syllabus requirement (P09); it gives no fallback rule so P06 does not fit.
units.anchor: The absence of GAI guidance in a course undermines the ability to recognize and adjudicate
units.policy: The absence of GAI guidance in a course undermines the ability to recognize and adjudicate instances of academic misconduct.
units.fit_note: Rationale: missing guidance undermines adjudication; no default rule stated.

units.why: 'each school maintains its own system, evidentiary standards, and procedures' states that schools run their own misconduct processes, which is P85 (units set their own rules).
units.anchor: each school maintains its own system, evidentiary standards, and procedures
units.policy: Each school maintains its own system, evidentiary standards, and procedures for identifying and adjudicating cases of academic misconduct.

units.why: Directs schools to check that honor codes and judicial frameworks can 'address academic misconduct with GAI', bringing AI misuse under integrity processes (P36).
units.anchor: the College and each school should ensure that existing processes and criteria in judicial frameworks
units.policy: The College and each school should ensure that existing processes and criteria in judicial frameworks and academic honor codes are adequate to address academic misconduct with GAI.
units.fit_note: Directs units to update integrity processes; does not itself classify AI misuse as misconduct.

units.why: Offers model honor-code wording: 'The unauthorized use of generative AI platforms by a student'. Unauthorized use is defined as misconduct, which is P36 (P61 does not fit as it defines AI, not misuse). Unit stance is restrict because use is allowed only when authorized.
units.anchor: The unauthorized use of generative AI platforms by a student
units.policy: The unauthorized use of generative AI platforms by a student, whether in the classroom, laboratory, studio, intern- and externships, independent research settings, or other spaces identified as serving educational goals, is an example definition of academic misconduct relative to GAI.

units.why: States a shared-responsibility principle: 'Instructors and students share responsibility for communicating about GAI use'. It spans P09 (instructor) and P78 (student), so neither alone fits.
units.anchor: Instructors and students share responsibility for communicating about GAI use.
units.uncovered_note: Principle that instructors and students jointly share responsibility for communicating and clarifying acceptable GAI use.

units.why: 'Instructors are responsible for communicating their policies and guidelines to students' puts the duty to communicate AI expectations on instructors; P09 fits.
units.anchor: Instructors are responsible for communicating their policies and guidelines to students.

units.why: Says materials 'need to include directions regarding the authorized use of GAI, including method(s) for disclosing or citing', a requirement to state expectations (P09) in syllabus, prompts or verbally.
units.anchor: need to include directions regarding the authorized use of GAI, including method(s) for disclosing or
units.policy: Instructional materials such as the course syllabus, assignment prompts, and verbal instructions need to include directions regarding the authorized use of GAI, including method(s) for disclosing or citing such use.

units.why: Sets a precondition for substantiating misconduct: the instructor 'should be able to demonstrate that students had a reasonable opportunity to know the rules'. This is an evidence standard for findings (P69), not a syllabus rule (P09).
units.anchor: The instructor should be able to demonstrate that students had a reasonable opportunity to know
units.policy: The instructor should be able to demonstrate that students had a reasonable opportunity to know the rules and expectations of the given context.

units.why: 'Students are responsible for requesting clarification when they are uncertain about the appropriateness of a given use' is the ask-when-unsure rule (P10).
units.anchor: Students are responsible for requesting clarification when they are uncertain
units.policy: Students are responsible for requesting clarification when they are uncertain about the appropriateness of a given use of GAI for a particular assignment, as well as when they have questions about maintaining academic integrity more broadly.

units.why: Students must show 'reasonable steps to know the rules and expectations regarding GAI', i.e. find out and follow the rules that apply (P78), rather than just ask when unsure (P10).
units.anchor: Students should be able to demonstrate that they took reasonable steps to know the rules
units.policy: Students should be able to demonstrate that they took reasonable steps to know the rules and expectations regarding GAI in a given situation.

units.why: 'AI detectors are principally problematic for the high numbers of false positives' says detectors are unreliable, which is P39.
units.anchor: AI detectors are principally problematic for the high numbers of false positives
units.policy: AI detectors are principally problematic for the high numbers of false positives they currently return (as of February 2025).

units.why: Warns that 'Sharing student work and data with AI detectors' raises privacy and IP concerns. P50 (protect personal data) is nearest; P49 is about students uploading course materials.
units.anchor: Sharing student work and data with AI detectors also brings up serious ethical considerations for
units.policy: Sharing student work and data with AI detectors raises serious ethical considerations for privacy, intellectual property, and adding student work to AI training materials.
units.fit_note: Concerns student work given to detectors by staff, covering IP and AI training use as well as privacy.

units.why: Sets what is not enough to find misconduct: 'AI detectors alone' cannot be 'a sufficient standard of proof'. P69 covers detector output as only supporting evidence; chosen over P39, which says detectors are not relied on at all.
units.anchor: should not allow for AI detectors alone to constitute a sufficient standard of proof
units.policy: Evidentiary standards for academic misconduct should not allow AI detectors alone to constitute a sufficient standard of proof.

units.why: Detector results 'may be included as evidence but are insufficient on their own': detector output as supporting evidence only, matching the broadened P69.
units.anchor: GAI detector results may be included as evidence but are insufficient on their own.

units.why: Names the kinds of evidence to weigh with AI detection: 'course materials, student work, credible witness accounts, and faculty expertise'. This is P69 (kinds of evidence to weigh).
units.anchor: Address multiple, possible sources of evidence for consideration in conjunction with AI detection
units.policy: Evidentiary standards address multiple possible sources of evidence considered in conjunction with AI detection, such as course materials, student work, credible witness accounts, and faculty expertise in their fields.

units.why: Principle statement: 'All students need equitable access to key resources when GAI is taught or used', matching P51 (equity and access). The privacy guidance half is coded in a later unit.
units.anchor: All students need equitable access to key resources when GAI is taught or used

units.why: Instructors using GAI 'are expected to ensure that all students have access to the necessary GAI tools', an equal-access duty (P51).
units.anchor: Any instructor whose course explicitly includes the use of GAI tools is expected to ensure
units.policy: Any instructor whose course explicitly includes the use of GAI tools is expected to ensure that all students have access to the necessary GAI tools.

units.why: Requires 'accommodations or ... accessible alternatives to their chosen GAI tools for students with disabilities'. P97 (accessibility) chosen over P51 because it is specific to disability access.
units.anchor: collaborating with appropriate campus partners
units.policy: The instructor is responsible for collaborating with appropriate campus partners (IS, CLASS, etc.) to implement accommodations or identify accessible alternatives to their chosen GAI tools for students with disabilities.

units.why: For fee-based tools, instructors 'should follow existing university processes for transparency about the cost'. This addresses cost of required tools (P51).
units.anchor: instructors should follow existing university processes for transparency about the cost of required course materials
units.policy: If any fee-based GAI tools are used for a particular course, instructors should follow existing university processes for transparency about the cost of required course materials.
units.fit_note: Requires cost transparency for fee-based tools; it does not say paid tools must not be required.

units.why: 'Instructors are asked to use university-licensed or university-recommended free tools whenever possible' points to institution-approved tools (P92); P17 is for one course's own tool.
units.anchor: Instructors are asked to use
units.policy: Instructors are asked to use university-licensed or university-recommended free tools whenever possible.

units.why: Asks instructors to 'Share university resources ... for protecting their privacy, as well as personal and university data', a data-protection practice (P50).
units.anchor: Share university resources for students that explain best practices for protecting their privacy
units.policy: Instructors share university resources for students that explain best practices for protecting their privacy, as well as personal and university data when using GAI tools.

units.why: University commitment to 'Building capacity and specialized knowledge of GAI among departments' handling accessibility; P97 covers accessibility of AI tools.
units.anchor: Building capacity and specialized knowledge of GAI among departments that typically respond to questions of
units.policy: The University will take a proactive approach to the accessibility of GAI tools by building capacity and specialized knowledge of GAI among departments that typically respond to questions of technology accessibility.

units.why: Commits the university to 'student-facing resources that identify common barriers to accessibility in GAI tools', which is P97.
units.anchor: Offering student-facing resources that identify common barriers to accessibility in GAI tools
units.policy: The University will take a proactive approach to the accessibility of GAI tools by offering student-facing resources that identify common barriers to accessibility in GAI tools and guidance on how to select tools that best fit the needs of students who use assistive technology.

units.why: Encourages using GAI as an accessibility aid: 'Consider ways to utilize the multi-modal capabilities ... to make materials and projects accessible'. P97 includes AI as an accessibility aid.
units.anchor: Consider ways to utilize the multi-modal capabilities of GAI tools
units.policy: Instructors, students, and staff consider ways to utilize the multi-modal capabilities of GAI tools to make materials and projects accessible to classmates and to a broader audience, e.g. generating a transcript for a podcast or video, generating written descriptions for a visual project.

units.why: The resource link points departments and instructors to 'accessibility testing for ... selecting new GAI tools'; it directs readers to further guidance (P115).
units.anchor: contact information for accessibility testing for departments and instructors selecting new GAI tools
units.policy: Technology Accessibility at WFU offers basic principles of digital accessibility and contact information for accessibility testing for departments and instructors selecting new GAI tools.

units.why: 'The University should empower instructors to investigate and explore GAI tools' through 'professional development opportunities': support for faculty learning (P63).
units.anchor: The University should empower instructors to investigate and explore GAI tools
units.policy: The University should empower instructors to investigate and explore GAI tools and to develop pedagogical skills for equipping their students to engage thoughtfully with the use and implications of GAI through a range of ongoing professional development opportunities.

units.why: Recommends leaders 'support the generation of GAI Discussion Frameworks among faculty', i.e. faculty communities that learn about AI (P63).
units.anchor: The AI Working Group for Academics recommends the Provost, Deans, and other academic leaders support
units.policy: The AI Working Group for Academics recommends the Provost, Deans, and other academic leaders support the generation of GAI Discussion Frameworks among faculty connected by school, department, area, or program.
units.fit_note: Faculty discussion groups at unit level; support is organisational rather than workshops or advice.

units.why: Recommends units 'plan for an ongoing way to continue to address GAI impacts', choose topics over time and report 'progress updates in annual reports'. It is about unit-level review and reporting, not revisiting a written policy (P54) or evidence gathering (P55).
units.anchor: We recommend that academic units plan for an ongoing way to continue to address GAI
units.policy: Academic units plan for an ongoing way to continue to address GAI impacts together, select individual topics to review over time, and give progress updates in annual reports.
units.uncovered_note: Academic units should plan ongoing discussion of GAI impacts and report progress in annual reports.

units.why: 'Students need clear guidance in every class regarding the permitted use of GAI technology' restates the clear-expectations requirement (P09) as a program discussion topic.
units.anchor: Students need clear guidance in every class regarding the permitted use of GAI technology
units.policy: Students need clear guidance in every class regarding the permitted use of GAI technology and its role, if any, in their learning and skills development.

units.why: 'clear communication about the consequences of inappropriate use' says handling of misuse should be stated up front, matching P123; P37 does not fit because no penalties are named.
units.anchor: they need clear communication about the consequences of inappropriate use of GAI technologies
units.policy: Students need clear communication about the consequences of inappropriate use of GAI technologies.

units.why: Asks instructors to seek 'consensus on approaches to GAI uses in multiple-section courses', aligning rules across sections (P109).
units.anchor: Program discussions should strive, where possible and relevant, for consensus on approaches to GAI uses
units.policy: Program discussions should strive, where possible and relevant, for consensus on approaches to GAI uses in multiple-section courses, especially those that serve as prerequisites to other courses.

units.why: Asks programs to consider whether 'additional or alternative measures for making learning visible' are needed because of AI, which is assessment redesign (P35).
units.anchor: how GAI may affect typical disciplinary assessments and demonstrations of learning
units.policy: A critical discussion topic includes how GAI may affect typical disciplinary assessments and demonstrations of learning and whether the projected impact requires additional or alternative measures for making learning visible.
units.fit_note: Discussion prompt about possible redesign, not a required redesign.

units.why: Honor-code and judicial bodies 'may set new expectations for GAI-related academic misconduct', so schools set their own AI integrity rules (P85); faculty are told to review them.
units.anchor: these groups may set new expectations for GAI-related academic misconduct
units.policy: Faculty should review guidelines from school/College honor codes and judicial frameworks; these groups may set new expectations for GAI-related academic misconduct.

units.why: Resource list entry 'CAT syllabus statement examples' supplies sample syllabus language, which is P110.
units.anchor: CAT syllabus statement examples
units.policy: The Center for the Advancement of Teaching provides syllabus statement examples (WFU).

units.why: 'CAT tools for developing GAI use policies' is an institutional template or tool for instructors; P110 is the nearest type.
units.anchor: CAT tools for developing GAI use policies
units.policy: The Center for the Advancement of Teaching provides tools for developing GAI use policies.
units.fit_note: Tools for building a policy, not only sample statements.

units.why: Restates the expectation that 'instructors have a responsibility to ensure ... equitable access to tools and resources, including options for disability accommodations', an equity rule (P51).
units.anchor: instructors have a responsibility to ensure that students will have equitable access to tools and
units.policy: University expectations state that when GAI is taught or used in assignments, instructors have a responsibility to ensure that students will have equitable access to tools and resources, including options for disability accommodations.

units.why: Suggests programs agree on common tools because it 'improves equitable access' when fee-based platforms are required; the stated reason is equity (P51).
units.anchor: Agreement on using the same tools across courses in the curriculum, where possible, also improves
units.policy: Agreement on using the same tools across courses in the curriculum, where possible, improves equitable access, especially if multiple courses in the same program require the use of fee-based GAI platforms.
units.fit_note: Recommends agreeing on common tools across a program's courses.

units.why: Recommends departments 'include instruction in GAI use and best practices somewhere in their curriculum', curricular AI literacy (P70); P44 is the career-skill argument and this sentence's reason is students' existing use.
units.anchor: the AIWG strongly recommends departments include instruction in GAI use and best practices somewhere in
units.policy: As students are already using GAI across all disciplines, the AIWG strongly recommends departments include instruction in GAI use and best practices somewhere in their curriculum.

units.why: Says AI may be inappropriate in some courses and asks instructors to 'be aware of GAI use across their shared curricula', aligning with colleagues (P109).
units.anchor: GAI may not be an appropriate learning or skills development tool in all courses
units.policy: GAI may not be an appropriate learning or skills development tool in all courses, but program instructors should be aware of GAI use across their shared curricula.
units.fit_note: Awareness of other courses' use rather than aligning rules.

units.why: Discussion question: 'How can or should the program coordinate GAI learning across courses', asking units to coordinate across courses (P109).
units.anchor: How can or should the program coordinate GAI learning across courses
units.fit_note: Discussion question about coordinating AI learning (reinforcement and duplication) rather than aligning rules.

units.why: Prompts programs to decide where GAI does or does not 'enhance learning in this field/discipline', tying AI decisions to learning aims (P83).
units.anchor: Identify ways GAI is best used or not used to enhance learning in this field/discipline.
units.fit_note: Discussion prompt, not a rule.

units.why: Asks what skills students need 'to use GAI successfully in relevant fields, disciplines, or professions', treating AI use as a professional skill (P44).
units.anchor: Identify the skills and approaches necessary to use GAI successfully in relevant fields
units.policy: Programs identify the skills and approaches necessary to use GAI successfully in relevant fields, disciplines, or professions, and how fields and professions use GAI that students should learn about.

units.why: Asks whether 'standards for verifying and citing results obtained by GAI' should be taught; verification (P31) is the nearest type.
units.anchor: Are there standards for verifying and citing results obtained by GAI that should be taught
units.policy: Are there standards for verifying and citing results obtained by GAI that should be taught in your curriculum?
units.fit_note: Covers both verifying and citing results as curriculum content; it is a question.

units.why: Asks whether GAI is part of 'the program’s learning outcomes', linking AI to learning objectives (P83).
units.anchor: Is GAI a part of the program’s learning outcomes now or in the future?
units.fit_note: Question about whether AI is itself a learning outcome.

units.why: 'All faculty should be aware of the increasing number of ways faculty may choose to use GAI' tells faculty to keep up with AI developments (P102).
units.anchor: All faculty should be aware of the increasing number of ways faculty may choose to
units.policy: All faculty should be aware of the increasing number of ways faculty may choose to use GAI to enhance all aspects of their work, along with the opportunities and the risks that GAI technologies provide.

units.why: Prompts discussion of faculty AI use 'in teaching support work (outside the classroom, such as preparing syllabi, designing assignments, grading ...)', which is P59.
units.anchor: Identify and discuss the ways faculty might use GAI in teaching support work
units.policy: Programs identify and discuss the ways faculty might use GAI in teaching support work outside the classroom, such as preparing syllabi, designing assignments, grading, writing letters of recommendation, and in administrative tasks.
units.fit_note: Discussion prompt about faculty uses; no use is permitted or banned.

units.why: Faculty AI use should be guided by 'meaningful and person-centered faculty-student engagement', guarding against displacing human interaction (P121); P59 covers which tasks, which this sentence does not name.
units.anchor: commitment to meaningful and person-centered faculty-student engagement should guide these applications of GAI technology
units.policy: In line with the Statement of Principles, commitment to meaningful and person-centered faculty-student engagement should guide these applications of GAI technology.
units.fit_note: Constraint on faculty AI use to protect faculty-student engagement.

units.why: Asks programs to consider 'ethical considerations guiding these uses', weighing values before using AI (P118).
units.anchor: What are the ethical considerations guiding these uses of GAI technology?
units.fit_note: Discussion question.

units.why: Asks about 'expectations for disclosure of GAI usage' in faculty work, the instructor-disclosure type (P47).
units.anchor: What are the expectations for disclosure of GAI usage in these contexts?
units.fit_note: Question about disclosure expectations; recipient of disclosure is not specified.

units.why: Directs faculty doing 'administrative and operational work' to the Administrative Use Guidelines for security, licenses and procurement: administrative AI use (P76).
units.anchor: faculty should consult the university
units.policy: In performing administrative and operational work for the university, faculty should consult the university's Administrative Use GAI Guidelines, especially for considerations of information and data security and privacy, university licenses and contracts, and procurement processes for purchasing GAI tools.

units.why: Asks about 'emerging professional standards ... for GAI in research, publishing, citation, and ... authorship', i.e. AI in research and scholarship (P62).
units.anchor: What are emerging professional standards in our fields for GAI in research, publishing, citation, and
units.policy: What are emerging professional standards in our fields for GAI in research, publishing, citation, and intellectual and creative authorship?
units.fit_note: Discussion question.

units.why: Describes how the guidelines were made: the Provost's Office 'organized an Artificial Intelligence Working Group for Academics that met from November 2023-February 2025' and reported in March 2025 (P84).
units.anchor: organized an Artificial Intelligence Working Group for Academics
units.policy: The Provost's Office organized an Artificial Intelligence Working Group for Academics that met from November 2023-February 2025, and its final report was delivered to the Provost and Deans in March 2025.

notes: Only document screened include. No school or computing-unit policy found per collect file. Discussion Framework questions were coded as informs or should discussion prompts with fit_notes.
